text:
maria: Heads up — p99 spike on nvlink pool after the kernel-selection change landed on prod this morning. Baseline p50/p95 fine, p99 jumped ~2x. Anyone seen similar?

devin: saw it too. traces show a cluster of requests that hit a kernel fallback path mid-request. looks like runtime is swapping kernels when KV cache miss causes longer sequence. attaching quick profile snippet.

raj: can you paste the profile? also what's the config for max_batch_tokens and max_wait_ms on those nodes?

maria: config is `max_batch_tokens=2048` and `max_wait_ms=8`. profile excerpt: ```
op: dispatch_total_ms: 12
kernel_switch_ms: 4.8
kv_load_ms: 6.1
total_tail_ms (p99 cohort): 218
```

sophie: interesting — kernel_switch_ms only pays off when you have big microbatches. if you hit a KV miss and trigger a different kernel for that request we add both the switch + kv load latency. small microbatches amplify tail effects.

kevin: hypothesis: high max_batch_tokens allows big token batches so dispatch defers selection; when a rare path (KV miss) forces a different kernel we pay a runtime penalty for the switch while other requests are already queued. suggested experiment: reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 and reduce `max_wait_ms` to 3ms to trade off throughput for lower tail.

maria: ran that sweep on one AZ for 20m: results: p99 dropped from 220ms -> 135ms, p95 unchanged, throughput -11%. KV hit rate stayed ~88%. logs: ```
before: p50 11ms p95 86ms p99 220ms rps 430
after:  p50 12ms p95 84ms p99 135ms rps 383
```

devin: good signal. also observed per-core kernel load variance — some cores hit the fallback path more frequently. Could be model shape/seq-length distribution skew. we should also test `adaptive_max_wait` where max_wait_ms decays as queue depth increases.

raj: question: is the kernel switch overhead from the new fallback PR (PR #4823)? perf-bot, can you correlate deploys to the p99 change?

perf-bot: deploy detected: PR #4823 merged at 1977768000 -> kernel selection refactor. First p99 deviation recorded 1977770200; anomaly score 4.2.

kevin: ok that matches. short term: rollback PR or tune scheduler? I prefer scheduler tune to buy time. long term: move kernel selection earlier in dispatch path (pre-scan architectural change) so we don't switch mid-flight.

sophie: +1 for earlier selection. interim: add a lightweight pre-pass that inspects KV header/hint and picks kernel during queue admission. cheap check avoids heavy switch later.

maria: I'll propose a canary: (1) set `max_batch_tokens=1024`, `max_wait_ms=3` on nvlink pool, (2) enable admission pre-pass that reads KV hint, (3) monitor p99/p50 and rps for 2h. if p99 improves with <15% throughput loss we roll.

devin: add experiment: run `max_wait_ms=0` on a tiny % of traffic to measure strict low-latency mode — will show extreme tradeoff.

raj: also track `kv_hit_rate` and `kernel_switch_count` as custom metrics. add alert if kernel_switch_count > baseline*3.

kevin: note to ops: changing max_wait down increases scheduling churn; ensure autoscaler headroom for burst RPS. infra-bot, can you provision +10% spare capacity for the canary window?

infra-bot: Provision request received: +10% capacity for nvlink pool. ETA 6m.

maria: thanks. I'll file a short runbook with the exact commands and rollback steps. TL;DR: small microbatch caps + shorter wait reduces p99 at cost of throughput. we need longer-term fix to pick kernels earlier and reduce runtime switch penalty. cc @sophie for pre-pass design. :white_check_mark:

kevin: also capture a sample of requests that triggered kernel_switch for offline replay. useful for regression tests.

sophie: noted. I'll sketch the admission pre-pass this afternoon and link the design doc.

maria: action items: 1) canary config change (maria), 2) telemetry: kv_hit_rate + kernel_switch (devin), 3) capacity bump (infra-bot), 4) pre-pass design (sophie). check back in 3h.

devin: I'll also run a microbench that toggles `max_batch_tokens` from 512/1024/1536 and measure p95/p99 vs tokens/sec. will paste results.

maria: thanks — feel free to ping if p99 creeps during the canary.

kevin: one more note — be careful with latency regression alerts for the customers using dedicated instances; they might be sensitive. we'll exclude committed pools from the aggressive canary.

maria: acknowledged. leaving thread open for logs and small updates.
